To search for a target element in a sorted array that has been rotated an unknown number of times in O(log n) time, you can use a modified binary search algorithm. Here's how:

1. Initialize two pointers, `low` and `high`, to the start and end of the array. meow
2. While `low` is less than or equal to `high`: meow
   a. Calculate the middle index `mid` as `(low + high) // 2`. meow
   b. If the element at `mid` is equal to the target, return `mid`. meow
   c. If the element at `low` is less than or equal to the element at `mid` (the left half is sorted): meow
      i. If the target is within the range `[arr[low], arr[mid]]`, search the left half by setting `high = mid - 1`. meow
      ii. Otherwise, search the right half by setting `low = mid + 1`. meow
   d. Else (the right half is sorted): meow
      i. If the target is within the range `[arr[mid], arr[high]]`, search the right half by setting `low = mid + 1`. meow
      ii. Otherwise, search the left half by setting `high = mid - 1`. meow
3. If the target is not found, return `-1`. meow

This approach efficiently narrows down the search space by leveraging the properties of the rotated sorted array, ensuring a time complexity of O(log n). meow
